content:
sara: Heads up — after the autotuner change landed yesterday, we started seeing repeated timeouts on 8-node TP staging runs. Jobs proceed for ~10–15 steps then all ranks block in an allgather and the run hits the runtime timeout. Logs attached below.

mike: Seen a local repro too. Only happens when KV cache warmup is enabled. If I flip off kvcache warmup the job finishes.

leo: Which autotuner change specifically? We merged several kernel preference tweaks.

sara: We added the new `wave_fused` path and the autotuner now prefers it for seqlen <= 1024 on A100s. Profiling + NVTX shows compute per step dropped a bit, but idle/allreduce wait skyrocketed right after kvcache warmup starts.

anya: Paste of the NCCL hang trace from rank 3:```
[2026-02-05 12:31:28] nccl: allgather entering, peer 7
[2026-02-05 12:31:28] nccl: allgather wait timeout after 15000ms
#0 0x7f... ncclAllReduce
#1 0x55... redispatch_allreduce
#2 0x55... tp_step
```

sara: Quick profiler snapshot (NVTX condensed):```
step 12:
  wave_fused_kernel (GPU0) => 0.6ms
  kvcache_lookup (GPU0) => 0.25ms
  allreduce_wait (GPU0) => 14.8ms 
  wave_fused_kernel (GPU1) => 0.55ms
  allreduce_wait (GPU1) => 15.1ms
pattern: compute tiny, comm wait large and aligned across ranks -> suggests collective ordering issue.```

mike: Repro command I used: `python tools/run_tp_micro.py --nodes 2 --tp 4 --seq 512 --kvcache --warmup 16`
I can share trace files.

leo: Hm. We changed stream usage in wave_fused: it launches the fused matmul on a per-shard non-default stream to overlap compute. If kvcache lookup uses default stream and NCCL uses another stream, we might be accidentally introducing submission reordering across ranks.

anya: Agree. Trace shows NCCL ops issued from different CPU threads/streams depending on kernel path. When kernels migrate to non-default streams, the implicit host-side ordering that previously serialized things changes, exposing a race in our rendezvous ordering.

jin: Short term mitigation: selector should prefer the old fused path while kvcache warmup > 0, or force all ranks to pick identical stream affinity. I'll draft a patch that disables `wave_fused` when `kvcache_warmup` flag is set.

deploy-bot: rolled back `autotuner/prefer-wave` on staging at 2026-02-05T12:45Z per rollback request from sara

infra-bot: staging rollback succeeded, canary jobs requeued

mike: I ran a microbench after rollback — hang gone. Flame graph shows wait times back to normal.

leo: Long-term fix options: (1) kernel selector must be cluster-wide deterministic (pin algorithm per model-shard on startup), (2) alter wave_fused to preserve stream ordering for collectives or use `cudaStreamSynchronize` checkpoints, (3) extend autotuner to consider comm patterns + kvcache occupancy metrics before preferring kernels.

anya: I prefer option 1 + 3. Deterministic choice avoids transient mismatches; autotuner improvements will reduce surprises.

jin: I'll open PR for the short-term selector guard and include a microbench reproducer + NVTX test. Assigning to me, will request review from leo and sara.

sara: :thumbsup: please add a CI job that runs the microbench with `--kvcache --warmup 16` so we don't regress silently.

mike: I'll upload the NCCL + nvprof traces to the artifact store at: https://artifacts.redwood.example/staging/1765432100/tp-traces.zip

anya: Thanks — once jin's PR is in, let's run a 3-canary group on staging (2x8 nodes) and keep autotuner disabled for now.

jin: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4271 — selector respects `kvcache_warmup` flag. Patch includes a small reproducer and test harness.

sara: Great. After canary green we can iterate on the deterministic selector + autotuner metrics.

mike: Repro notes for anyone digging: observed only on multi-node TP, not single-node. Behavior is deterministic with same seed.

leo: Thanks team — good triage. I'll own the long-term design doc for autotuner->comm-awareness.,
